# Two surfaces, one controller layer

| | Dashboard | Mobile |
|---|---|---|
| Prefix | `/api/v1` | `/mobile/v1` |
| Token ability | `dashboard` | `mobile` |
| Client | `Frontend/` (React) | `Mobile app/` (Flutter) |
| Route file | `Backend/routes/api.php` | `Backend/routes/mobile.php` |
| Platform admin (`/platform/*`) | yes | **no** — not registered at all |
| Invitation management | yes | **no** |

Login mints the ability from the prefix it arrived on, so a token is not replayable across
surfaces (`AuthenticatedSessionController::abilityFor`). Both surfaces share controllers —
a fix in a controller fixes both, and a **contract change breaks both**.

## When you change a shared controller

1. **Change the controller once**, then check both route files still express the intended
   contract (`Route::get('thing', …)` on each).
2. **Update both clients**: the React page/type and the Flutter model/datasource. A new
   response field is additive (safe); a renamed or removed field is breaking.
3. **Check the mobile board entity** specifically. `RequestBoard` in
   `Mobile app/lib/features/requests/domain/entities/service_request.dart` mirrors the
   buckets the dashboard renders — if the API gains a bucket, both clients must show it or
   items silently vanish from the mobile Today page.
4. **Add tests on both surfaces.** `Backend/tests/Integration/Surfaces/ClientSurfaceTest.php`
   asserts that a dashboard token is rejected by `/mobile` and vice versa, and that the
   platform console is absent from `/mobile`.

## Things that must never drift

- The platform console stays off the mobile surface. Mobile has no landlord concept.
- Invitation management stays on the dashboard only; the app can accept an invitation
  (`POST /mobile/v1/auth/invitations/accept`) but not issue one.
- Token abilities are checked with `abilities:dashboard` / `abilities:mobile` on every
  authenticated group.
- `/mobile` requests also pass through the `api` middleware group, so tenant identification
  and throttling behave identically.

## Quick parity check

```bash
cd Backend
php artisan route:list --path=api/v1     --json | ConvertFrom-Json | Select-Object -ExpandProperty uri
php artisan route:list --path=mobile/v1  --json | ConvertFrom-Json | Select-Object -ExpandProperty uri
```

Compare the two lists. Anything tenant-facing present on one and missing from the other is
either a deliberate omission (platform, invitations, member role changes) or a bug — say
which, in writing, when you report.
